title: Use of Micro X-ray Computed Tomography with Phosphotungstic Acid Preparation to Visualize Human Fibromuscular Tissue
protocol: Draw an incision line on the cadaver to indicate the cutting area for sample harvesting.
Extend the incision line medially to a medial canthus, laterally to a lateral canthus, superiorly to the superior border of the lower eyelid, and inferiorly to 1 cm below the orbital rim.
Cut facial tissues following the incision line with a blade.
Ensure the cut is deep enough for the tip of the blade to touch the bone.
Include skin, subcutaneous tissue, muscle, fat, and periosteum in the sample.
Fix the sample in 10% formalin immediately after harvesting.
Preserve the fixed sample for 5 to 7 days at room temperature.
Slice the sample into 3 pieces (5–7 mm in thickness).
Sew the superolateral side of each piece using a needle and black thread.
Place the sample in 70% ethanol until staining.
Prepare 210 mL of 70% ethanol solution and add 2.1 g of PTA power to it.
Mix well using a shaker at 55-60 rpm.
Fill three 70 mL plastic containers with the PTA solution.
Soak the specimens into the containers and place them on a shaker for effective penetration.
Leave the samples for 5–7 days.
Store the sample in 70% ethanol to prepare for scanning.
Wrap the sample with parafilm to prevent drying.
Place the sample on the tray of the scanner.
Set the source voltage to 70 kV.
Set the source current to 114 μA.
Select an Al filter thickness of 0.5 mm.
Set the image pixel size to 20 μm².
Configure the pixels setting to 2240 × 2240.
Set the exposure time to 500 ms.
Set the rotation step to 0.3 degrees.
Start scanning the sample.
Open the dataset using the reconstruction software.
Select Ring artifacts reduction of 7.
Set Beam-hardening correction to 40%.
Begin reconstruction by selecting Start on the Start tab.
Launch the file resizing software.
Choose Source data set as the input files.
Select jpg format for the output destination.
Apply a Resizing option of 1/2 with No interpolation (fast).
Adjust the slide bar in Image compression to 100 (highest).
Start converting the files.
Run the 3D volume rendering software.
Select Actions > Load volume data to launch the dataset.
Adjust the brightness and contrast level by modifying shape transfer function in histogram in the Transfer Function Editor tab.
Select Options > Lighting.
Select Shadows and Surface Lighting icons.
Move (click and drag), rotate (right-click and drag), and zoom in or out of (scroll) the model.
Slide the plane (shift + click and drag in the inner direction) to show sectional images.
Turn on Light icon.
Adjust the lighting indication bar and find the best lighting for viewing.
Turn off the Light icon.
Select Options > Show > Clipping Box to hide the box for the final image.
Select Actions > Save image to store the image.
